headline: A 24-13 lead leaked at Mile High; the Jets get the 10-point reply

sectionTitles.currentState: 5-2, a wild-card seat, and the fixes
sectionTitles.gamePlan: Jets at Arrowhead on a 10-point number

dek: Kansas City is 5-2 after Denver won 28-24, and the next kickoff is vs the New York Jets on Sun Nov 8, 12:00 PM CT on CBS with the Chiefs laying 10.
videoHook: They had 24-13 and the ball moving, then Denver closed 28-24 — now the Jets walk into Arrowhead as a 10-point home price.
theEdge: ESPN FPI lists Kansas City at 80.4 percent to beat the Jets, and DraftKings has the Chiefs minus 10 on a 46.5 total — a home number that still has to live with 10 quarterback hits and a 24-13 lead that finished 24-28.
editorNotes: Missed 54-yard field goal is a non-scoring drive result (H.Butker, wide right, Q4 2:36), not a scoring kick. Do not phrase it as a made kick.
Coleman 5-yard touchdown is named on the Q4 1:56 play-by-play; other scoring rows list player unknown, so those scorers stay unassigned.
Karlaftis forced the fumble; Trautman recovered for Denver. Team turnovers are 0-0. Zone blitz is a Jets call, not takeaway credit.
Possession: last game KC 31:29, DEN 28:31. Prior Seattle KC 24:09, SEA 35:51. Team rush last game 90, not Walker's 69.
Afternoon kickoff window: the words night and nights are omitted from the edition.

pressConferences.title: Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes & Chris Jones Postgame Press Conferences - NFL Week 8

storyline.lede: Kansas City spent the Denver afternoon ahead and still left Empower Field at 5-2.
body: The box does not read like a team that was outgained. Denver sat at 294 yards, 2-of-11 on third down, 28:31, and still scored the last two touchdowns.

The leak was operational. Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal wide right at Q4 2:36 with the score 24-21. Jonah Coleman then scored from 5 yards up the middle at Q4 1:56. The last Kansas City snap of the game was a turnover on downs after Jaylon Moore's false start wiped a play, the sequence Reid later tied to the ball spotter and a fourth-and-goal look.

Arrowhead Pride's updated picture puts the Chiefs in the wild-card mix, with Buffalo at 6-1 atop the AFC and Denver listed ahead of Kansas City. Brett Veach is already looking for a receiver before the trade deadline. The football answer this week is simpler than the roster debate: protect Mahomes, finish drives, and treat the Jets as a real assignment under a minus-10 price, not a victory lap.

lastGameReview.label: Week 8 · Sun, Nov 1 · 3:25 PM CT
lastGameReview.lede: At Empower Field, Denver led 3-0 on a 39-yard field goal at Q1 9:43, Kansas City answered with an 11-yard touchdown at Q1 6:04, and the clubs traded the rest of the way until Coleman’s 5-yard touchdown at Q4 1:56 made it 24-28.

analysis.body: The scoring order is the film. Denver’s 45-yard field goal at Q2 14:08 made it 7-6. Kansas City’s 73-yard touchdown at Q2 7:40 made it 14-6. Denver’s 1-yard touchdown at Q2 1:15 made it 14-13, and Harrison Butker’s 45-yard field goal at Q2 0:19 sent it to the half at 17-13. The 4-yard touchdown at Q3 1:38 built 24-13. That was an 11-point lead. Denver’s 2-yard touchdown at Q4 8:55 cut it to 24-21.

Mahomes’ line was efficient and unfinished. He was 30-of-41 for 321 yards and three touchdowns, sacked twice, rating 120.1, with net passing at 309. Emmett Johnson finished with 5 catches for 128 yards and a touchdown on 6 touches. Rashee Rice had 7 catches, Travis Kelce 5, Kenneth Walker III 4 catches to go with 21 carries for 69 yards. The team rush was 90 yards on 24 attempts, not Walker’s line alone as the club total. Xavier Worthy had 3 catches. Cyrus Allen had 2.

Denver earned the close. Bo Nix was 20-of-32 with one sack, a 103.9 rating, and three rushes. The Broncos rushed for 77 on 23 attempts. Coleman had 15 touches and the named 5-yard scoring run up the middle. Courtland Sutton caught a 23-yarder; Jaylen Waddle caught a 35-yarder. Third down was 2-of-11, so this was not a conversion parade. It was two fourth-quarter finishes plus field goals of 39 and 45.

Steve Spagnuolo’s unit created a George Karlaftis sack and a forced fumble that Adam Trautman recovered for Denver, so the box stays at zero turnovers for both clubs. Kansas City was flagged often: Kristian Fulton pass interference, Jack Cochrane unnecessary roughness, Kelce false start, Reid Thomas offside, Fulton illegal block, Trey Smith holding, Drue Tranquill face mask, Alohi Gilman pass interference and a later unnecessary roughness, Jacob Canady holding, and Moore’s false start at Q4 0:04. Denver had its own flags, including Sutton offensive pass interference. The missed 54-yard attempt and the final turnover on downs decided a game the yardage column had already tilted Kansas City’s way.

takeaways.title: The lead was real, the finish was not
takeaways.body: 24-13 after the Q3 1:38 touchdown should have been a manage-and-close script. Denver scored at Q4 8:55 and Q4 1:56. A missed 54-yard field goal at Q4 2:36 sat between those two scores.

takeaways.title: Explosives traveled; the run did not carry the afternoon
takeaways.body: Johnson’s 128 receiving yards and a 73-yard team touchdown gave the offense vertical punch. Walker’s 21 carries produced 69 yards inside a 90-yard team rush. That is volume without a downhill cushion.

takeaways.title: Pressure and flags taxed the operation
takeaways.body: Mahomes absorbed 10 quarterback hits and two sacks. Kansas City recorded two hits and Karlaftis’ sack. The penalty list, not a turnover column, is where the self-inflicted damage shows up.

whatWorked: Mahomes at 30-of-41, 321 yards, three touchdowns, 120.1, and a clean turnover column
Johnson as the receiving leader at 5 catches, 128 yards, and a touchdown, with Rice (7) and Kelce (5) in the catch count
Karlaftis’ sack and forced fumble, even with Trautman recovering for Denver
whatDidnt: An 11-point lead after 24-13, followed by Denver touchdowns of 2 and 5 yards
Butker’s missed 54-yard field goal, wide right, at Q4 2:36
10 quarterback hits and two sacks on Mahomes
Moore’s Q4 0:04 false start and a final turnover on downs
A 90-yard team rush on 24 attempts after Walker was asked for 21 of those carries

currentState.lede: The Chiefs are 5-2 after a 5-0 start and two losses, Seattle 20-3 and Denver 28-24. The offense just posted 399 yards and still needs a close. The next assignment is a home favorite’s job against the Jets, not a referendum on the whole season.

workOn.title: Protection before the shot
workOn.body: Ten quarterback hits and two sacks on a 30-of-41 day is the install item for Eric Bieniemy. Screens and defined quick concepts have to travel with the 321-yard passing line, or the Jets will not need a perfect coverage plan.

workOn.title: Finish a lead without a special-teams bailout
workOn.body: Reid called the Denver loss self-inflicted. The tape agrees: 24-13, a missed 54-yard attempt at 24-21, then Coleman from the 5. Late-game operation has to include a cleaner fourth-down presentation than Moore’s false start.

workOn.title: Early-down run that matches the touch count
workOn.body: Walker touched the ball 25 times and gained 69 on 21 carries. Team rushing was 90. Against a club laying 10, empty early downs turn a 6-of-14 third-down rate into another sweat.

workOn.title: Penalty clusters on passing downs
workOn.body: Fulton and Gilman pass interference, plus holding and false starts, gave Denver extra plays. Spagnuolo cannot spot a defense that already held Denver to 2-of-11 on third down and still watch free yardage on flags.

thinkAbout.title: Is the receiver market a need or a panic
thinkAbout.body: Veach is looking before the deadline, and Allen just posted a season-high snap load with two catches. Rice, Kelce, Johnson, and Worthy already produced catches. The staff should separate a depth add from a story that the skill group vanished.

thinkAbout.title: How hard to lean on the kicker
thinkAbout.body: Butker missed from 54, wide right, in a one-score game, and he has acknowledged the mistake. Fourth-down aggression and field-position choices this week should assume that 50-plus is a debate, not an automatic.

thinkAbout.title: Wild-card math versus an AFC West hole
thinkAbout.body: Denver holds the division lead Kansas City relinquished. Buffalo is 6-1 in the picture Arrowhead Pride posted. A home win does not restore the West by itself. It does stop a third straight loss.

gamePlan.lede: The Jets come to GEHA Field at Arrowhead on Sun Nov 8, 12:00 PM CT on CBS, with Kansas City laying 10 and the total at 46.5. ESPN FPI has the Chiefs at 80.4 percent. That price is the assignment: play like a favorite in the first 20 plays, then finish the way Denver did not allow.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Kansas City’s last honest tape is a 399-yard, zero-turnover offense that still lost a fourth-quarter lead, against a defense that held Denver to 2-of-11 on third down and 294 yards and still gave up 28 points on finishes. The Jets do not need to replicate Denver’s fourth-quarter script if Mahomes is hit 10 times again or if Walker’s 21 carries stay stuck near 69 yards. Matchup leverage is protection, early-down identity, and red-zone cleanliness.

keys.title: Make the minus-10 number boring
keys.body: Script Walker inside on early downs, then let Mahomes throw defined answers to Rice, Kelce, and Johnson. A 46.5 total does not require a track meet. It requires Kansas City to own the down-and-distance chart the way the 31:29 possession suggested they could.

keys.title: Steal the rush with the screen and the mesh
keys.body: Ten hits is the scouting report the Jets will carry. Spacing to Walker, who already had four catches, and mesh with Rice and Kelce, keeps the 2-sack issue from becoming the story of the favorite.

keys.title: Two deep, then a called zone blitz
keys.body: Denver still hit a 23-yard Sutton catch and a 35-yard Waddle catch. Cover-2 is the shell that takes the cheap shot away. The zone blitz is a Spagnuolo call to change the picture, with Karlaftis as the featured rusher, not a retroactive credit for the Trautman recovery.

keys.title: Special teams and the last snap are football
keys.body: Do not spot the Jets a missed long field goal or a false-start wipe in a four-point game. If it is fourth-and-goal, the presentation has to be clean before the call is clever.

script: Open under center with Walker on inside zone and a Mahomes keep only if the picture is clearly there; he had two rushes in Denver, including a 4-yard scramble.
Second series: mesh to Rice and Kelce, Johnson as the vertical tag, Worthy on the perimeter.
If the Jets heat shows, throw the screen to Walker or Johnson before asking for another 73-yard shot.
Third-and-medium: defined quick game, not a hold-and-hunt that feeds another hit.
Defensively, Cover-2 on early downs, zone blitz on an obvious passing down with a lineman dropping.
Inside the 10, huddle the protection and the eligible report. Hunter Nourzad’s lone listed report was Q4 15:00. Do not improvise a jumbo look that was not in the call sheet.

spotlight.title: 24-13 was the game Kansas City had
spotlight.body: The 4-yard touchdown at Q3 1:38 made it 24-13. Denver’s next two touchdowns, 2 yards and Coleman’s 5, made it 24-28. Reid’s self-inflicted label fits the missed kick and the late false start better than it fits the 399 yards.

spotlight.title: A 10-point home price after two losses
spotlight.body: DraftKings has Kansas City minus 10 with a 46.5 total. FPI is at 80.4 percent. The number assumes the Denver offense tape travels and the Denver finish does not.

spotlight.title: Johnson’s 128, Rice’s seven, Allen’s snaps
spotlight.body: Johnson led receivers with 128 yards and a score. Rice had seven catches. Arrowhead Pride’s snap count notes a season-high workload for Cyrus Allen, who finished with two catches. Veach is still shopping the position.

spotlight.title: Wild card, not the West lead
spotlight.body: The playoff wire has Buffalo at 6-1 and Denver ahead of a 5-2 Kansas City club. Week 9 does not repair the division. It keeps the wild-card path from getting thinner.

matchups.chiefs: Patrick Mahomes, 30-of-41, 321 yards, 3 TD, 2 sacks, 10 hits
matchups.opponent: Jets pass rush, unnamed in this packet
matchups.note: The Denver tape says the ball comes out accurately and the quarterback still absorbs 10 hits. Until the protection answer shows, the favorite’s edge is the arm, not the pocket.

matchups.chiefs: Kenneth Walker III, 21 carries, 69 yards, 25 touches; team rush 90 on 24
matchups.note: Touch volume is already a weapon. The Jets have to fit 21 carries plus four catches or Bieniemy will live on schedule.

matchups.unit: Chiefs skill group vs. man and zone
matchups.chiefs: Johnson 128 and a TD, Rice 7 catches, Kelce 5, Worthy 3
matchups.note: Four pass-catchers already have a role. Mesh and vertical tags do not require a new name to stress a defense.

matchups.chiefs: 2 QB hits, Karlaftis 1 sack, opponent third down 2-11 in Denver
matchups.note: Denver scored 28 on 294 yards because of finishes, not because third down was a parade. Cover-2 plus a called zone blitz is the plan to keep explosives and goal-line runs from stacking.

matchups.chiefs: Butker made a 45-yard field goal and missed from 54 wide right
matchups.opponent: Jets special teams and field position
matchups.note: One made 45 and one missed 54 in the same game is not a settled unit. The Jets can win field position if Kansas City treats 50-plus as automatic.

xsandos.title: Walker on inside zone to open the count
xsandos.situation: First-and-10 at Arrowhead, before the Jets can set a pass-rush menu off the 10-hit Denver tape
xsandos.why: Walker already carried 21 times for 69 inside a 90-yard team rush. A minus-10 home script needs that volume on schedule so Mahomes is not throwing third-and-long after a 6-of-14 conversion day.
xsandos.coaching: Bieniemy: zone steps, one cut, Walker downhill. Mahomes carries the keep as a constraint, not a habit — he had two rushes in Denver. Do not declare a gap the call sheet has not named.

labels.te: zone combo to the second level

xsandos.title: Screen the 10-hit rush
xsandos.situation: After a heavy Jets rush look, or second-and-6-plus when the pocket picture matches Denver’s two sacks
xsandos.why: Mahomes was accurate at 30-of-41 and still took 10 hits. Walker’s four catches and Johnson’s five give Bieniemy two screen targets who already touched the ball.
xsandos.coaching: Let the line release and lead. Throw it on time. This is an answer to heat, not a trick. Worthy can occupy the perimeter so the screen alley stays clean.

xsandos.title: Mesh for Rice and Kelce
xsandos.situation: Third-and-medium against man, the down Denver’s flags and hits kept stealing
xsandos.why: Rice caught seven and Kelce five in a game Kansas City still lost on finishes. Rubs give Mahomes a defined throw so the 120.1 rating is not built on held balls.
xsandos.coaching: Crossers at depth, sit if the defender trails, Walker as the checkdown. Johnson can bend a seam tag if the linebacker chases the mesh.

xsandos.title: Four verts off the Johnson tape
xsandos.situation: Second-and-short after a Walker carry, when the Jets squeeze the box to stop 21-carry volume
xsandos.why: Johnson’s 128 yards and a touchdown, plus a 73-yard team score on the Denver sheet, say the vertical answer is already in the lineup. Worthy and Allen give the outside and seam pictures without inventing a new starter.
xsandos.coaching: Seams bend to the hash. Outsides run past the corners. Mahomes takes the open middle if it is there and the checkdown if the safeties stay high. Do not label the throw play-action; the Denver scoring rows do not say play fake.

xsandos.title: Cover-2 to erase the cheap explosive
xsandos.situation: Jets first-and-10 and second-and-medium, the downs where Sutton’s 23 and Waddle’s 35 still happened against this defense
xsandos.why: Denver managed 28 points on 294 yards and 2-of-11 on third down. The explosives and the finishes did the damage. Two deep, five under takes the shot away and lets the rally tackle show up.
xsandos.coaching: Spagnuolo: corners sink, safeties stay deep, linebackers fit the run. Nick Bolton and the second level rally. This shell is the constraint before any heat is shown.

xsandos.title: Zone blitz as a called change-up
xsandos.situation: Jets obvious pass, third-and-6 or longer, after Cover-2 has shown for a series
xsandos.why: This is a call to use against the Jets, not a claim about how the Denver fumble happened. Karlaftis already has the sack on the stat line. A simulated pressure lets a second-level rusher arrive while a lineman drops into the zone Denver’s crossers tried to stress.
xsandos.coaching: Show heat, drop a defensive lineman, rush from the second level. Tackle the checkdown. Do not tell the room this call created a takeaway last week — Trautman recovered that fumble for Denver.

labels.te: hook replace from the rush look

coaching.detail: Reid used Monday to talk about self-inflicted issues after 28-24, including the fourth-and-goal operation and the ball spotter. That is the staff lesson, not a yardage apology.
A 120.1 rating next to 10 quarterback hits means the call sheet has to include answers that come out before the rush arrives. Screens and mesh are the practical install.
Holding a club to 2-of-11 on third down and 294 yards is real defense. Giving up a 2-yard score and Coleman’s 5-yard score up the middle is the red-zone item for the Jets.

personnel.detail: Brett Veach is looking for a wide receiver with the deadline approaching. The Denver catch sheet already includes Rice, Johnson, Kelce, Worthy, and a season-high snap load for Cyrus Allen.

Arrowhead Pride’s snap-count note flags a season-high workload for Cyrus Allen in the 28-24 loss. He finished with two catches. That is a role to define against the Jets, not a snap total this desk will invent.

strategies: Lean on Walker’s 25 touches early so the minus-10 script is not a dropback parade.
Pair Johnson’s vertical production with mesh throws to Rice and Kelce.
Use the screen as the answer to a rush that just put 10 hits on Mahomes.
Play Cover-2 before showing the zone blitz, and treat the blitz as a change-up.
Keep 50-plus field goals a conversation after the missed 54.
Clean the fourth-down presentation so a false start cannot wipe the last idea of the game.
debates: Does 399 yards and a 120.1 rating mean the offense is fine and the close is the whole problem?
Should Veach add a receiver this week, or is Allen’s snap jump the internal answer?
How aggressive should Reid be on fourth-and-goal after the Empower Field finish and the ball-spotter explanation?
Is minus 10 the right price for a 5-2 team that just blew an 11-point lead?
Does the wild-card path change the urgency of the Jets game, or is any third straight loss the same problem?
